answers.note: The assumption test now also asserts slugify('Håkon Ørsted') === 'hakon-rsted', pinning that 'ø' has no ASCII base and acts as a separator rather than folding to 'o'.

The shape test keeps the equality for 'Ünïcode & Numbers 123' and now applies the /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ regex to slugify() of every non-empty case in the suite (plain, whitespace, accented, punctuation, hyphen-wrapped, 'Straße', 'Håkon Ørsted'), each with a message naming the title, so the assertion can fail independently of the equality.

The doc comment now says that only the combining diacritical marks U+0300-U+036F are dropped after NFD decomposition, and that any combining mark outside that block acts as a separator like the other non-ASCII characters.
